content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text uses Matthew 1:16's admitted two readings as the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, which is the single-verse ambiguity ground K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings, with nothing else settling it, is such a verse.","room":"I interpreted 'A verse that admits both readings, with nothing else settling it, is such a verse' and weighed whether it lets an unresolved ambiguous verse support UNDERDETERMINED or instead bars that ambiguity from grounding UNDERDETERMINED.","why":"Because the judge's stated ground for UNDERDETERMINED is that a single verse admits both readings, K-S2 forbids that ground."}
